en: In Numa, visitors will be concerned with the Hours honoured by the Sisterhood of the Knot. [As long as this card remains, Numatic visitors will have an interest in <sprite name=grail> or <sprite name=nectar> Mysteries. Their needs will usually be more exacting than visitors who come during more traditional seasons.]

In Numa, visitors will be concerned with the tricks and strategems that might have been used in secret by the Hours. [As long as this card remains, Numatic visitors will have an interest in <sprite name=moon> Mysteries. Their needs will usually be more exacting than visitors who come during more traditional seasons.]

In a hidden fold of the mountains above the city of Cluj lies the enigmatic relic they call Saint Mihail's Coffin. Decades of patient work have finally breached its outer shell. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=knock> or <sprite name=moon> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

In a highly specialised clinic in an obscure corner of the capital, specialists study the ecstatic agonies of the case known only as'the Open Reverend', who once was the vicar of the parish of St Agnes Forestreet. The blessings of St Agnes of the Fires and St Agnes of the Shears are ungentle. But St Agnes of the Threshold may be her cruellest aspect...  [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=heart> or <sprite name=winter> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

In the drier reaches of the Bounds, the Légion du Seuil keeps a brutal peace. Perhaps even a necessary one. But the Légion recruits from among the Bounds-beasts. How trustworthy is it, really?  [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=edge> or <sprite name=grail> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

In the hissing wastes of sand where once stood a city called Miah… another man has died. But he almost made it out. He made it far enough that a goatherd found him, raving to the end about gardens, with a flower crushed in his hand. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=moth> or <sprite name=rose> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

Like many criminal enterprises, Reckoners offer loans to the desperate and unwary - but Reckoners can offer loans not only of cash, but of allotted years of life. They usually keep a low profile, but now two Reckoner mobs have gone to war in the unremarkable Lithuanian city of Kaunas. Why? What's in Kaunas? [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=moon> or <sprite name=edge> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

Messana: a prosperous little desert village that has become, in recent years, a place of pilgrimage. There have been peculiar manifestations there of late - villagers gifted with sight, or struck blind. The Church has despatched its representatives to investigate. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=lantern> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

No-one has ever successfully staged an entire performance of 'Wings Within Wings'. That's probably why they call it the Invisible Opera. But now someone is trying again. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=grail> or <sprite name=moth> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

Oriflamme's Auction House is never robbed. But what if it has been? What if, somehow, priceless treasures have been replaced with pricey forgeries? How could we even be sure? [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=knock> or <sprite name=forge> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

Sailors have a term for the compass-whirl phenomenon which occurs before sightings of the city Ys. They say a compass has caught 'the giddy horizons'. There is something of a giddy epidemic in the North Sea this year. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=rose> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]
Someone would like to know something.

The 'Lyterion', a faddish health camp in the Black Forest, has attracted attention after many of its clients seem to have developed sudden, sometimes upsetting, artistic abilities. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=heart> or <sprite name=nectar> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

The Ligeian Medusa is long dead, as is well attested. It's nevertheless well-attested also that she walks the streets of Budapest by moonlight. That's just one of those things. But now, for the first time, she's being glimpsed in daylight too. What could that portend? [Visitors with an interest in or Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

The New King has sanctioned the use of the Crown's wealth to fund a visionary new industrial project - one that will transform our economy, and furnish the kingdom with a sense of patriotic mission. Parliament, dazzled, has already passed the Royal Endeavour Act, mandating the construction of the necessary facilities, although the details remain in some respects vague. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=forge> or <sprite name=lantern> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]

The Suppression Bureau has a growing interest in the recent fad for unconventional - often prophetic - religious movements. No laws have been broken. Nothing sinister has come to light. All these movements are comfortingly Solar in nature. But there does seem to be something going on. [Visitors with an interest in <sprite name=winter> or <sprite name=lantern> Mysteries will want to talk about this.]
Ice raps on the roofs and tree-tops.
In this country the sky is rarely clear. The Sun goes courteously cloaked.
The Sun is not what it was, but today he is smiling.
The gentlest of earth tremors. Just to remind us that the earth is not dead but sleeping.
The world is pale today. 'The White is west of the world, and winter does not wait forever', Solomon Husher once said.
Trees bend, walls creak, travellers bend low against the blast.

'Picasso? I'll give you Picasso.' [The Artist came to Hush House to shape and share a History of primal, ultimate, unprecedented experience; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Bosk Wisdom.]
Dull-gleaming yellowish stones. Amber? I feel that I should know...
Goatskin? Antelope? Some scarred leather that catches at my memory. I should know.

I am the Librarian of Hush House, and this journal will be my Perpetual Map. [The Cartographer's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to chart a new History in which their impossible map would be possible; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Nyctodromy Wisdom.]

I am the Librarian of Hush House, and this journal will record what arose from my Crime and my Curse. [The Archaeologist's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to record a History where their crime could be forgiven... or redefined. But you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Skolekosophy Wisdom.]

I am the Twice-Born Librarian of Hush House, and this is the journal in which I keep my remaining memories. [The Twiceborn's 'third choice' might be life as the Librarian, or it might be something more radical. But you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Illumination Wisdom.]

I have striven to be the last Librarian of Hush House. This journal records my strivings. [The Revolutionary's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to carve out a new History where the most fundamental law would be overthrown; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Horomachistry Wisdom.]

I laid so many of those uncanny things to rest. I thought it was right. I fear now it was not. I am the Librarian of Hush House, and here I will ensure they will be remembered. [The Executioner's dearest wish, when they came to the House, was to record a new History which will atone for their crimes; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Preservation Wisdom.]

I was rich; but something was missing. I am no longer rich... and still, something is missing. Hush House is a place of conclusions, and here, as Librarian, I may find mine. [The Magnate came to the House to conclude a History where they will find peace; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Hushery Wisdom.]

I've crossed three oceans and almost drowned in one. Now I am the Librarian of Hush House. Perhaps here I will be safe from my parents; but I can't take that for granted. [The Prodigal's dearest wish is sanctuary - as Librarian, or in a History where things are different;but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Ithastry Wisdom.]

In Caer Adar I heard the secret gods speak one to another. I thought that would be the end of my journey, but the more I heard, the more I knew must be missing. I am the Librarian of Hush House, and I will find what has been lost. [The Symurgist came to Hush House to find a History with the songs that have fallen to silence; but you can complete the game by recording any History. You might wish to begin your studies with the Birdsong Wisdom.]
Is that real silver? I feel that it should be. I should remember.
The binding is unusual - and half-familiar - some kind of silk? It's survived its soaking remarkably well.
The cover is unusual. Horn? Bakelite? Chitin? I should be able to remember.
The feathers that adorn its cover are bedraggled from its time in the sea.
The heavy metal cover nearly took me down with it. But I survived, and so will this.
The one possession I kept from the shipwreck. It must be important to me. [The Aspects below tell you more about how and where you can use this item. Hover over them to learn more.]
The scaled binding has survived the soaking well enough.
The unusual metal binding is untouched by the sea.
A moment in time. In another moment, it'll be gone. [If unused, Memories disappear with the dawn.]
Light leaks in where, from, how. [An unusual and versatile lesson that will NOT PERSIST PAST DAWN. Use it quickly.]
Someone's time is up, and now they're going home.
[This memory has become part of something else.]
'A Knowledge in the Look of Things'
A niche with a plaque: 'Not to be crossed, and not to be found'
A niche with a plaque: 'Whereof we cannot speak, thereof we must remain silent'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who brought a key long lost'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who commanded the raising of this stair'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who departed, but did not forget'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who died not but passed within'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who dwells still in the three-flowered tree'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who knew cages'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who often purified, but was not often pure'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who returned loyalty for loyalty and curse for curse'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who returned to complete what he began.'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who saw his fate, and did not shirk it'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who saw what had not yet passed'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who served two masters as best he could'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who was born of three nations, and of none'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who was denied victory, though never defeated'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who was feared more than he merited'
A niche with a plaque: 'Who was mocked more than he merited'

Eleventh Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
Fifth Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
First Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
Fourth Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
If I have a successor, their image might stand here.
If it doesn't live on the wall or on the floor, it's probably a thing.
If it goes on the floor, we call it a 'comfort', whether or not it's comfortable.
Ninth Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
Second Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
Seventh Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
Sixth Librarian of the Curia of the Isle
Tenth Librarian of the Curia of the Isle

Thirteenth Librarian of the Curia of the Isle?
This, of course, would be me. I could use whatever I want as my image.

[Keep things here until you tidy them away.]
A tiny treasure dropped carelessly into the tin!
Acquiring a Memory: A Stolen Secret
Someone has tucked a glinting lens into one of its eye-sockets.
Someone has tucked a sad little treasure beneath the seat cushion…
The candle is much heavier than it should be. Something has been sealed into the wax…
The pumpkin bears the marks of intrusion. It's been filled with something sticky and unexpected.
What's this down the back of the cushions? A small and unexpected treasure.

[You can only keep five things in your belongings. A sixth item will be abandoned unless it already has a home. Abandoned items will wait for you outside the House.]
'I promise to pay the Bearer on Demand the Sum of Five Pounds'. The Bearer never does demand, though.
A noble paper in soothing green. Britannia lounges on her throne, flaming hammer propped insouciantly across her knee.
Five shillings; one-quarter of a pound.
Half a pound; but not half a note. A recent innovation.
Or 'thruppence', or a 'thruppenny bit'. Like twopence, but more so.
Or, if you prefer, 'tuppence'. A sort of Janus of pennies.
Swirls and curlicues in solemn hues. Until recently, one could exchange bank notes for gold in the banks of the capital. A seven-pound note can still be exchanged for rarer metals in rarer places.
The silver coin of least value - but silver, nonetheless.
The smallest denomination coin, except for the smaller ones.
This could use different levels to indicate the amount paid.
Twelve pence or, if you prefer, one-twentieth of a pound.
Two and a half shillings. Obviously.
BOOK OF HOURS is a gentler game than Cultist Simulator - you can save and load at will.
Before the Curia, before the Dewulfs, before the Church of the Unconquered Sun, the sisters of the Knot kept their secrets in the caves of the Isle.
Click a slot to highlight everything that can go over it; mouse over an Aspect to highlight everything with that Aspect.
Commit Skills to the Tree to get more Soul cards... and also to develop your understanding of the world and the Histories.
D-Pad down pauses; right and left modify the game's speed; you can change these controls in Settings.
Hit BACKSPACE to cycle between workstations with finished recipes.
House furnishings are sometimes unique. Resources are not. If you destroy a resource, you can always get a replacement eventually.
Hush House is one of the nine great libraries of the Watchman's Tree - the select few places where the Hours sanction the preservation of forbidden knowledge.
If you think you've hit a dead end, try something else. There's always a way forward, although it may take you in a different direction than you had planned...
If you used up your starting ink, don't worry. There are lots of inkpots in the House, and you can learn to brew your own ink.
If you're new to BOOK OF HOURS... you might not realise just how far you can zoom in with the scroll wheel.
If you're new to BOOK OF HOURS... you might not realise just how far you can zoom in with the touchscreen.
Left stick and left trackpad move the cursor; button A or trackpad tap to interact with objects and rooms. Right stick moves your view around (you can also use the touchscreen).
Left-click to interact with objects and rooms; right-click or use cursor keys to move your view around (you can change keys in Settings).
Push R1 to cycle between workstations with finished recipes.
Save your game if you're worried about what might happen next
Space pauses; numpad + and - change speed up and down; you can change these keyboard shortcuts in Settings.
Tap on a slot to highlight everything that can go over it; tap on an Aspect to highlight everything with that Aspect.
The Good, the Bad, the Ugly
The Librarian has left the world behind. This has its advantages, but also its price.
The icons at the top of the Workstation window suggest relevant Powers to use in recipes at that workstation.
The seasons will pass; don't worry. There's no need to hurry... except in Numa.
Thirza Blake, Seventh Librarian, spent all the House's money on her projects before her disappearance... and that's when Nocturnal Branch stepped in.
Weary wrist? R2 + tap sends to the nearest workstation; L2 + tap to the nearest verb; you can change these controls in Settings.
Weary wrist? Shift-click sends to the nearest workstation; ctrl-click to the nearest verb; you can change these keyboard shortcuts in Settings.
When upgrading a Skill, you can use a Lesson from any skill if it matches at least one Aspect... and you only need one Lesson. The rest can be any matching Memory.
You can't destroy it by accident, but if you put it on the wrong shelf, you might be vexed. This is an accurate simulation.

'The Aleppine': Historian, doctor, and above all, traveller. The good doctor has been associated with all but one of the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. He was even Secretary Nunciant of Hush House for a little while, but he has never been on good terms with the Suppression Bureau.
Agdistis and Chaima have become friends.
Al-Adim and Connie will see each other after the salon.
Arthur and Douglas will keep in cautious contact.
Arthur will be keeping an eye on Coquille.
Artist, socialite... burglar? An unspeakably charming woman with a particular knack for getting adopted.
Arun and Coquille have developed a cautious amity.
Arun and Denzil have discreetly established an affinity.
Arun and Yvette will leave together tonight...
Businesswoman, chess-master, initiate of the scarred Hour sometimes called the Colonel.
Chaima and Zachary have something almost like a friendship.
Collector of proverbs, connoisseur of wines, herald of the Hour called Mare-in-the-Tree.
Connie has risen swiftly in the Suppression Bureau, to the exalted rank of Constable-Oculate Minor. Don't get in her way.
Coquille and Douglas are not friends - not quite.
Detective-Illuminate of the Suppression Bureau. A stoic, but weary, fellow. His dearest wish is to move to Chingford and grow roses. But the buggers won't let him retire.
Douglas has learnt to tolerate Hokobald better than most.
Essayist, illustrator, critic. Editor of the Kerisham Review.

Exile, riddlemonger, Thunderskin devotee. ('I'd rather say confidant.') Impeccably dressed, but always in dark clothing so the stains don't show. Dark the dressings too at his ankles and his wrists. ('I won't take a seat. It's kind of you to offer. It would be unkind of me to accept.')
For many years, under many names, Rowena has done, learnt, or eaten many things she really shouldn't have. But for many years, under many names, she's served as the protectress of Hush House.
Formerly; Ehsan was a healer; he was not human; he was Secretary Salvant of Hush House. But not all at the same time. Fussy, kind, famously foul to look upon.
Gräfin Friederike Dagmar Sophia Theresia Helena Benigna von Nagelsburg, if you prefer. She doesn't.
Hero, pilgrim, traitor. He'll always be a soldier, but never again can he be only a soldier.
Huntress, goumier, occasional Bureau consultant. When it can't be killed, and it really needs killing, Chaima's the one they turn to.
Magus, Winter-long, controversial philosopher. For an immortal exalted by an Hour of Silence, especially one who might be dead, he has had a great deal to say for himself over the years.
Manuscript-hunter, legacy-scavenger... mercenary? Many would question his ethics; few would deny his acuteness.

Marksman, detective, renegade. He has always been a quiet man, but since he left the Suppression Bureau, he has grown even quieter, and terribly still - except for his fingers and for his eyes, always in restless motion.
Metallurgist, gourmet, corrupted immortal. And, supposedly, a long-ago king's by-blow.
Morgen seems almost protective of Zachary.

Musician, mystic, impresario. Agdistis was a dancer once. One cannot see him without knowing it. The wound in his thigh keeps him from the stage; but his every movement still has the cadence of a prayer.

One-time Librarian of Hush House, one-time Librarian of the Invisible Serapeum in Alexandria, and currently... what, exactly? Serena is close-mouthed, but I know that she has worked with the St Rhonwen Trust.
Philanthropist, collector, former Librarian. A complicated man, but not a cruel one.
Playwright, philologist, psychoanalyst: as happy with questions as with answers.
Priest, diplomat, gardener: a soft-voiced man with a very steady gaze.
Rakehell, dilettante, infuriating prodigy. Possibly dead, possibly real.

Socialite, yachtswoman... and, under the name 'Morgen', an alukite, a Ligeian. The former means, among other things, that she eats people. The latter means, among other things, that she is not to be taken lightly.
There's something between Azita and Yvette, although exactly what remains to be seen.
'And your weather. Your weather is also a disappointment.'
'As God wills, I suppose. (Don't ask me which God!)'
'I arrive hungry. I leave famished. Someone will regret that... but not you, not today.'
'I can't believe we used to fund this place.'
'I know the House has been through hard times. But though much is taken, much abides, does it not? Another time.'
'Mm. Well, no doubt we shall see each other again.'
'Never mind. The traveller is always returning, no? So if I come back later, am I returning then? Or am I returning now?'
'Not to worry! Nice to get a bit of sea air.'
'Oh, sweetie. I'm not disappointed, just... well, perhaps I'm a little disappointed.'
'So much has been lost, hasn't it? I don't envy you. Good luck.'
'Sometimes, the end comes sooner. Sometimes, there's no damned end to it at all.'
'That's the bloody thing about bloody libraries.
